approved_text: Let p_n denote the n-th prime. Is it true that there is a continuous function f: [0, ∞) → ℝ such that, for every c ≥ 0, the set of natural numbers n with (p_{n+1} − p_n)/log n < c has natural density f(c)?
draft: Let p_n denote the n-th prime. Is it true that there is a continuous function f: [0, ∞) → ℝ such that, for every c ≥ 0, the set of natural numbers n with (p_{n+1} − p_n)/log n < c has natural density f(c)?
source_docstrings:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
source_lean:
theorem erdos_234 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ, Continuous f ∧
    ∀ c : ℝ≥0, HasDensity {n : ℕ | primeGap n / log n < c} (f c)
